project.author: WarpForge Examples
project.description:
A minimal newsletter-signup form designed to be converted to a single reusable Composite Block. Open the project, right-click the wf_window block → "Save as Composite Block…" — the whole wf_window → wf_screen → header → input → button → footer tower becomes one custom block named e.g. `wf_custom_signup_widget` that you can drop into any project. To inline it back, right-click the composite → "Expand here". The on-click handler is a separate top-level stack you can wrap independently as `wf_custom_save_email_handler`.

Why this shape: every wf_ui_* widget has prev/next connectors and the whole UI lives in one chained tower, so a single block is all the wrapper needs. Sprite-stage projects can't do this because their click hats are separate stacks.

workspace_state.blockly_xml:
<xml xmlns="https://developers.google.com/blockly/xml">
<block type="wf_window" id="window_main" x="40" y="40"><field name="TITLE">Newsletter Signup</field><field name="WIDTH">420</field><field name="HEIGHT">320</field><next><block type="wf_screen" id="screen_home"><field name="NAME">Home</field><field name="ROUTE">/</field><next><block type="wf_ui_header" id="ui_header"><field name="TITLE">Stay in the loop</field><next><block type="wf_ui_input" id="ui_email_in"><field name="PLACEHOLDER">your@email.com</field><next><block type="wf_ui_button" id="ui_subscribe_btn"><field name="LABEL">Subscribe</field><next><block type="wf_ui_footer" id="ui_footer"><field name="TEXT">We send one short email a week.</field></block></next></block></next></block></next></block></next></block></next></block>
<block type="wf_on_click" id="evt_subscribe" x="40" y="320"><field name="TARGET">ui_subscribe_btn</field><next><block type="wf_save_local" id="io_save_email"><field name="KEY">subscribed_email</field><field name="VALUE">ui_email_in</field></block></next></block>
</xml>
